[Date]

Fidelis Care  
[Appeals address or submission route listed by Fidelis Care]

Re: Appeal of Medical Necessity Denial  
Member: Casey Iverson  
Member ID: W207784190  
Reference number: POC-1ACF427871-17933  
Requested service: Partial knee replacement  
CPT: 27446  
Date of denial notice: August 25, 2026

Dear Fidelis Care Appeals Department:

I am appealing Fidelis Care’s denial of prior authorization for partial knee replacement, CPT 27446. The denial states that the imaging findings submitted do not support medical necessity.

The submitted clinical record supports the requested procedure as follows:

- I have experienced 24 months of progressive knee pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- My symptoms have persisted despite conservative treatment. I completed 16 supervised physical-therapy visits from May 14, 2026, through July 9, 2026, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion.
- I used NSAIDs for four months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 3, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- MRI performed on July 30, 2026, showed full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medial disease.
- My condition substantially limits function. I cannot climb stairs without assistance and awaken three to four times each night because of pain.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- The record does not identify active infection or untreated substance use. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.

The MRI directly documents advanced, compartment-specific structural disease corresponding to the requested partial knee replacement. The combination of full-thickness medial-compartment cartilage loss, bone-on-bone apposition, grade 4 medial radiographic disease, persistent pain, functional impairment, and failure of conservative treatment supports medical necessity for the requested surgery.

I request that Fidelis Care overturn the denial and authorize CPT 27446. Please have the appeal reviewed by an orthopedic surgeon or other reviewer with appropriate expertise in knee arthroplasty.

The public materials I was able to locate identify CPT 27446 as a knee arthroplasty procedure but do not provide the medical-necessity criteria used for this denial. I therefore request that Fidelis Care provide:

1. The exact medical policy or clinical-review criteria applied to this request;
2. The policy title, reference number, version or effective date;
3. The specific imaging findings and other requirements that Fidelis Care contends were not satisfied;
4. The clinical rationale for concluding that the July 30, 2026 MRI did not support medical necessity; and
5. Copies of any clinical-review materials relied upon in making the denial.

Please consider the enclosed prior-authorization records, including the MRI report, physical-therapy discharge note, medication and injection history, examination findings, and functional limitations.

Please send the appeal determination in writing to [mailing address]. If additional information is required, please contact me at [telephone number] or [email address]. Please also confirm receipt of this appeal.

Sincerely,

Casey Iverson  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]

Enclosures:

- Denial notice dated August 25, 2026
- MRI report dated July 30, 2026
- Physical-therapy discharge note
- Medication and corticosteroid-injection treatment history
- Orthopedic examination findings
- Prior-authorization clinical records
